subject: Information Theory
title: The Binary Symmetric Channel
description: A quick win: understand The Binary Symmetric Channel.

hook.text: Flip a biased coin for every bit you send. Heads: bit arrives correctly. Tails: it flips. That's the BSC model.

buildup.text: The binary symmetric channel has one parameter: the crossover probability p that any bit flips.

discovery.text: Shannon's channel capacity for the BSC is C = 1 − H(p), where H is the binary entropy function.

twist.text: Even at p = 0.1 (10% error rate), the capacity is 0.53 bits per channel use. Reliable communication is still possible.

climax.text: The BSC is the simplest noise model but captures the core challenge: random, independent bit flips.

punchline.text: A coin flip per bit. The simplest model of noise.

quiz.question: What does the crossover probability p represent in the BSC?
options: The probability that any single bit is flipped
